wstep: There is no recipe here for Korean-style cabbage with chili: JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for it.

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to Oregon State University Extension, a recipe for fresh or quick pack pickles must call for vinegar of 5% acidity and have at least as much vinegar as water, unless it is an OSU or USDA tested recipe.
Use only vinegar labelled 5% acidity; white and cider vinegar can be used interchangeably; do not use wine vinegars, homemade vinegar or lemon juice.
Untested recipes can be prepared and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks; do not store them on the counter.

akapity: A recipe from the hawaii.edu recipe archive (Chili Pickled Cabbage – Kim Chee) uses napa cabbage with equal amounts of white vinegar and light soy sauce and does not give the acidity of the vinegar.
According to that recipe, the sealed jar is left in a cool place for at least 24 hours before using, and it keeps for up to a week in the refrigerator.
Refrigerator pickles are not heat processed, so they must be kept in the refrigerator.
Cabbage is a vegetable, and all fresh vegetables except most tomatoes are low-acid foods with a pH above 4.6.
